parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, facility ban, border/document friction, or documented police targeting of trans visitors; same-sex conduct has been legal since 1933. Against this, the dossier is thin and dated: the only violence is a 2005 attack on a visiting drag group and a 2006 beating after which police refused the case, pre-dating the 2007 provision. That provision protects sexual orientation but not gender identity, leaving trans-specific recourse thin—a resident-facing gap, not a proven visitor exposure. Political hostility to LGBT expression is documented to 2015 (Pride-ban demand, parliamentary shaming), but organised pushback and petitions (20,000 for protection vs 1,262 against marriage) show substantial counter-mobilisation. No current prevalence or trans-specific incident is documented, so old attacks are weak evidence of present frequency. Net: no tier-1/2 exposure, but documented hostility and uncertain recourse keep it below the reduced-risk protections tier.
